title: The dove and the olive leaf (Genesis 8:6–12)
hookLine: the raven doesn't return; the dove comes back with a leaf

lines: SAILORS LOST AT SEA, A BIRD ON BOARD.
cards: Before radar and satellites, sailors lost at sea sometimes carried birds on board. When they couldn't see land, they'd let one go and watch. If it circled and came back, there was no shore within reach.
If it flew off in a straight line, they followed it. The ark has been floating for months. The rain has stopped, the waters are going down, and the box has come to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
But there's one window, and all Noah can see through it is sky. So he does what those sailors did, and lets a bird go.

teach.h: THE RAVEN GOES TO AND FRO.
teach.b: The first bird is a raven. In the King James Bible, it "went forth to and fro, until the waters were dried up from off the earth." It never comes back with news.
Ravens can live on what they find, even in a drowned world.
Then Noah sends a dove. She finds nowhere to rest her foot, and comes back. And there's a tender detail here: Noah puts out his hand, and takes her, and pulls her in.
A man who hasn't said a word in the whole story, reaching out the window for a tired bird. He waits seven days. He sends her again.
And this time: "And the dove came in to him in the evening; and, lo, in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth." One leaf.
Not a field, not dry ground under his feet. Just a single fresh leaf in a bird's beak. Olive trees are tough; they can come back from almost nothing.
And that leaf is enough for Noah to know. Something is growing again out there. He waits seven more days, sends her one last time, and she doesn't come back at all.

teach.h: YONAH: THE DOVE FOUND A HOME.
teach.b: Which is good news too: she's found a home. In Hebrew, dove is yonah, the same as the prophet Jonah's name.
And for Christians, the dove will return at the Jordan River, when the Spirit comes down on Jesus at his baptism like a dove.

teach.h: IN HER MOUTH WAS AN OLIVE LEAF.
teach.b: Centuries later, the dove with an olive branch became a picture of peace across the world. It started with one leaf at evening.

how: The dove appears across Christian art as a sign of the Holy Spirit and of peace, and in the catacombs of Rome early Christians drew a dove with an olive branch on tombs.

o: dove, the same word as the prophet Jonah's name
olive, the tree whose leaf the bird brought
raven, the first bird sent out from the ark

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: went to and fro, never came back
came back with an olive leaf

s: the first bird Noah sends out is a dove
it's a raven, which goes to and fro and never comes back with news.
the dove brings back a whole olive branch
the King James text says an olive leaf, "pluckt off".
Noah reaches out and pulls the tired dove back into the ark
he "put forth his hand, and took her, and pulled her in unto him into the ark."

games.q: you're Noah. the dove has come back with one fresh olive leaf in her beak. what do you know now?
o: nothing yet; a leaf is too small.
the waters are going down, and something is growing.
it's time to leave the ark today.
games.why: "so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth." one leaf is enough to know. he still waits seven more days.

practice: Think about the part of your life that still feels underwater, and don't look for dry land or the whole answer; look for a leaf. One small thing growing again: a better morning, a kind word, a bill paid, one honest conversation.
If you pray, you can give thanks for it.

wordCard.voice: Yonah. The Hebrew word for dove, the same as the prophet Jonah's name: the bird that came back with one green leaf.

orig.note: Hebrew: dove, also the name of the prophet Jonah.

carryVoice: Your line: a leaf is enough. The whole thing doesn't have to be fixed yet. That's day three hundred forty-five.
